facts.icd10_text: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter

statements.text: Back pain began 07/28/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 6 weeks before this visit.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/27/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.
Pain NRS 6/10 despite 5 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.
Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.
Approximately 33% loss of L3 vertebral body height.
Focal kyphotic deformity at L3 measuring 21 degrees.
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.
Fever to 38.9 C with elevated CRP; discitis at the fracture level is suspected.

Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/01/2026
Patient: Ela Adams, 74-year-old female

Subjective:
Ela Adams presents for her routine follow-up visit. She reports feeling generally well with no new complaints today. She denies any recent falls, trauma, or significant changes in her health status.

Objective:
Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows normal range of motion without tenderness or swelling.

Assessment:
Ela Adams is a 74-year-old female with stable health status at this time. No new issues identified.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine health maintenance. Encourage regular exercise and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any new concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 08/27/2026
Patient: Ela Adams, 74-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/27/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Approximately 33% loss of L3 vertebral body height.
Focal kyphotic deformity at L3 measuring 21 degrees.

Impression:
The imaging demonstrates an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L3 vertebral body characterized by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. There is an approximate 33% loss of vertebral body height at L3 with an associated focal kyphotic deformity measuring 21 degrees.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical presentation and patient status.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/07/2026
Patient: Ela Adams, 74-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 07/28/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 6 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 6/10 despite 5 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Course:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Current Concerns:
Fever to 38.9 C with elevated CRP; discitis at the fracture level is suspected.

Plan:
Further evaluation and management of suspected discitis will be prioritized. Continue osteoporosis treatment program and monitor clinical status closely. Consider imaging and possible biopsy to confirm diagnosis and guide therapy.
